title: Of Clemency

full_text:
On the seventh day, the Seventh Wazir demanded the execution of all who challenge royal authority. Bakhtiyar stepped forward and delivered an eloquent defense of clemency:

'Sire! Any barbarian can draw a sword and take the life of a fallen enemy; brute force requires neither wisdom nor greatness of soul. But to stay the hand when the sword is raised, to forgive when you have the absolute power to destroy, is the divine attribute of true kingship!

Vengeance only perpetuates the cycle of bitterness: the son of the slain man will harbor hatred, and his grandson will sharpen a dagger. Blood cannot wash away blood; only the sweet water of mercy cleanses the stain of enmity.

Clemency turns an enemy into a devoted defender, softens the hardest heart, and wins a victory that steel can never achieve.

The conqueror who slays his captives rules over corpses and slaves; but the monarch who pardons with magnanimity rules over the grateful hearts of free men, as shown in the history of King Bihkard.'
moral: Pardoning an adversary when you have the power to destroy him is the highest victory of a monarch.
